metadata.case_name: LEE HO CHUEN v. LAI WAI KEI

plaintiff.occupation_before: Taxi driver (since 1998); previously maintenance technician with Canadian Airlines
plaintiff.occupation_after: Worked part time as a locum taxi driver and part time as a clerical worker in a friend's fabric factory; later worked as a taxi driver full time at reduced capacity (20 days/month, resting periodically)

source: Urgent Computerized Tomographic scan of his brain revealed right sided chronic subdural haematoma.

injuries.description: haematoma at the right parietal scalp
source: Upon examination, it was found that he had a haematoma at the right parietal scalp

injuries.description: superficial abrasion on his right knee
source: superficial abrasion on his right knee

treatments_received: Ambulance transport to Accident and Emergency Department of Caritas Medical Centre
admitted to hospital for two days
computerized tomographic scan (CT scan) of brain
burr hole drainage for chronic subdural haematoma (operation lasted 5 hours)
follow-up outpatient treatment at Department of Neurosurgery of PYNEH

losses.description: Weakness of both lower limbs and residual effects (persistent headache, dizziness, post-concussion symptoms) affecting everyday life and working capacity

comparable_cases.case_name: Ip Shuk Hing v Yuen Yuk Wai
comparable_cases.injury_description: hairline fracture on the skull from a blow in the head, which resulted in haematoma and loss of consciousness. Mild post-concussion syndrome and mild post-traumatic stress disorder resulted. Symptoms of headaches, instability and dizziness.

comparable_cases.case_name: Tsui San Yau v Tsang Wai Hong
comparable_cases.injury_description: scalp laceration, facial swelling and left shoulder abrasion. Diagnosed with anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder. Post-concussion syndrome diagnosed because of headache and dizziness; mild head injury and an adjustment disorder.
